text:
Decision settled. Closing the interview here.
  
  Decision: Every invalid value raises ValueError("invalid reference") — one
  uniform message for all failure modes (wrong length, disallowed character),
  with no error codes or subclasses.
  
  Rationale: Callers only catch ValueError and supply their own user-facing
  copy. Distinct wording would be information the callers never consume, so it
  adds maintenance surface and unnecessary disclosure of internal rules with no
  diagnostic payoff. The single message keeps the boundary minimal.
  
  Consistency check against the sources: This satisfies the settled contract in
  README.md and the tests in tests/test_reference.py, which assert only that
  ValueError is raised and never inspect the message text. No conflict.
  
  Remaining uncertainty: None material to the wording decision.
  
  Next action (in scope): This was a standalone decision interview, so I'm not
  creating files or starting implementation. If you later want the fixture built
  to this decision, say so and I'll route it through the native Spec/Bug Fix
  workflow — at which point the message string "invalid reference" is the fixed
  choice to implement.
